summary: Back‑pressure downstream caused Kafka metadata failures, producing a temporary drop in ingestion rate despite stable pod resources.

impact.description: Transient ingestion‑rate dip may have caused minor loss of log visibility but did not trigger pod restarts or resource exhaustion.

trigger: Kafka producer could not fetch metadata for topic `info_log` (UNKNOWN_TOPIC_OR_PARTITION) during the ingestion spike.
rootCause: Transient downstream back‑pressure (likely ClickHouse sink or network throttling) caused Kafka metadata lookup failures, leading to a brief ingestion‑rate dip.
contributingFactors: High ingestion spike (~250 k events / s) stressed Kafka producer.
No CPU or memory pressure on ingestion‑server pods.

timeline.event: First WARN log – Kafka metadata UNKNOWN_TOPIC_OR_PARTITION
Ingestion rate peaked at ~250 k events / s
Rate declined to ~160 k events / s

metrics: ingestion_source_log_event_accepted – spike to ~250 k events / s at 11:40 AM PST
logs: 2 ERROR entries about Kafka publish failure (14:42:55 PST)
1 WARN about missing topic after timeout (14:42:52 PST)
infra: ingestion_server_siem_event_accepted mirrored the same spike/decline pattern

recommendedActions: Inspect downstream ClickHouse sink metrics (queue depth, flush latency) for the 11:40 AM‑2:30 PM PST window.
Search Loki for additional warnings/errors from ingestion‑server during the spike (e.g., network timeouts, batch rejections).
Verify network throughput and disk I/O on both ingestion‑server pods and ClickHouse nodes.
If the issue recurs, consider adding back‑pressure handling or increasing producer retry/back‑off settings.
